note: Each flag is an open irregularity. None blocked publication. Each names what was observed, what is missing and what would close it.

flags.title: Short codes do not match the ASINs they resolve to
flags.detail: Three unique short links were supplied. Each resolves to a real Amazon listing, but no short code equals the ASIN it lands on, and all three codes are 9 characters where Amazon defines an ASIN as 10. Example: link.amazon/B0hmGG4m2 resolves to /dp/B08FKW9JRM. The code is therefore a redirector identifier, not a product identifier, and copying it into an ASIN field would corrupt the record.
flags.action: Close by confirming the intended ASIN inside the enrolled Associates workflow for each link, then recording it in the intended_asin field. Until then the intended fields stay empty and the observed values stand alone.

flags.title: No tracking tag observed on any resolved destination
flags.detail: The destinations were reached with Amazon session and referrer parameters present, but no tag parameter carrying the selected tracking ID shopnow047c-20 was observed. Tracking is the mechanism that creates a commission at all: the Associates Agreement defines Special Links as links that properly use the tagged link formats, and the Participation Requirements require the Associates ID to appear in the URL of each link placed on a site.
flags.action: Close by generating each link inside Associates Central with the enrolled tag, confirming the tag appears in the destination URL, then confirming the click appears in the tracking report before scaling. Do not assume the supplied links are non-compliant — the point is that compliance was not observable from outside the account.

flags.title: Account rate card is behind a sign-in; public category rates do not say what these three items pay
flags.detail: The rate-card address in the Program Policies Appendix redirects to an Associates sign-in whose return address is the account's own custom rate card (re-read 2026-11-21). A separate public page does publish category-level fixed rates (Table 1): Kitchen 4.50%, Home / Home Improvement / Tools 3.00%, All Other Categories 4.00%. That table does not say which category each of the three observed listings is paid under (the paper towel holder and the pot rack both sit under Home & Kitchen › Kitchen & Dining), and the Policies say the effective rate can differ slightly from the rate described in an account's rate card. No per-product rate, earnings estimate, revenue forecast or conversion score is therefore published; the Spec & policy audit shows the public category rates as a reference only. Correction: earlier records on this site said no rate could be read anywhere; that was wrong for the public category table and is corrected here and in S03/S13.
flags.action: Close by reading the custom rate card inside the enrolled account, then confirming category attribution for each ASIN from a first-party earnings report after real orders. Any published figure must also state that Amazon may change rates at any time.

flags.title: Six of nine register fields cannot be verified from outside an account
flags.detail: Price verification, rating verification and Special Link validation all require either API enrolment or an Associates account. Two of them are additionally constrained by policy: price may only be displayed when Amazon serves the link or the data comes through the Product Advertising API, and star ratings may not be displayed at all unless obtained through that API. Price tracking and alerting are prohibited outright. The register shows these columns as unverified rather than filling them.
flags.action: Price and rating columns close only with API enrolment. Link validation closes with account access per F02. None of the three may be filled by inference in the meantime.

flags.title: One submitted link was duplicated
flags.detail: Four link lines were supplied but only three unique URLs. link.amazon/B03QDuGdo appeared twice. It is recorded once and flagged, so that the catalogue does not show a phantom fourth product.
flags.action: Closed as an intake observation. No further action unless a fourth distinct product was intended, in which case that link has not yet been supplied.

flags.title: All four suggested titles are published as method checklists, but no verified appliance listing exists to attach
flags.detail: The suggested hypotheses concern basket and oven-style air fryers, air fryer capacity, cleanup trade-offs and multi-function kitchen appliances. No air fryer or appliance listing is in the supplied catalogue, so writing product-specific guides would require inventing specifications. The first title is published as the air fryer guide. Updated 2026-11-21: the remaining three are now published as well, as specification-free method checklists (air-fryer-capacity.html, air-fryer-cleanup.html and multi-function-appliances.html). Each states on the page that it is a method and not a test, quotes no specification, price or star rating, recommends no model and carries no buying link. The guides index keeps the four working titles in a table so the record of what was supplied stays visible. None is a claim about popularity, search volume or product superiority.
flags.action: Still open in one respect: with no verified air fryer or multi-function appliance listing, none of these pages can carry researched specifications or a sponsored link. Close by supplying verified listings, at which point the checklists become the place those specifications go.

flags.title: Attribution makes a link hop unavoidable, and that hop is a policy edge case
flags.detail: Amazon's Commission Income Statement disqualifies purchases where a customer reaches Amazon through a link that passes through an intermediate site without a click or affirmative action there — a Redirecting Link. That is the standard server-side click-tracker pattern. This site therefore sends the outbound click as a beacon and lets the browser go directly to Amazon, so no session is ever routed through this domain and no intermediate-site hop exists.
flags.action: Closed by design, but flagged because the alternative — the common redirect-through-your-own-domain pattern — would have created the risk. Worth re-reading if the analytics implementation ever changes.

flags.title: The contract behind the affiliate relationship was accepted outside this build
flags.detail: Participation requires an accepted Operating Agreement and a site that was identified in the application. This build can neither see nor verify the account's enrolment state, the site list on the application, or whether the tracking ID shopnow047c-20 is active and attached to this domain. All three are asserted by the account holder, not verified here.
flags.action: Close by confirming in Associates Central that the account is active, that this site URL is listed on the application, and that the tracking ID matches. Also confirm the six-month sales requirement and the disclosure obligation are being met from the account side.

flags.title: Publication cadence is set but the next issue is not written
flags.detail: This build establishes a cadence and ships a feed, a sitemap and a publishing checklist. The second issue did not exist when this flag was written. Nothing on the site claims a publishing frequency that has been sustained. Updated 2026-11-21: issue 02 has now shipped with three method checklists, and standards.html carries a publication log of what shipped and when. Two consecutive issues on schedule still have not been demonstrated, so the flag stays open.
flags.action: Close after two consecutive issues ship on schedule. Topic selection should be driven by measured queries once an analytics endpoint is configured, which it currently is not.

flags.title: Measurement is shipped but not switched on
flags.detail: The five defined events are implemented and the outbound counter is a non-blocking beacon, but the script ships with an empty endpoint. Until a collector is hosted and configured, events are logged to the browser console and discarded. The site therefore reports no measurement today and claims none.
flags.action: Close by hosting a collector, setting data-endpoint, and verifying each of the five events arrives. Do not enable a third-party analytics vendor without revisiting the privacy page first.

flags.title: The brief describes an automated agent; the Program Policies now regulate agents that use Program Content
flags.detail: The Program Policies, last updated April 14, 2026, add Agent Terms to the IP License (section 4). An Agent is any software or service that takes autonomous or semi-autonomous action on behalf of a person. If an Agent accesses Program Content it must identify itself in the user-agent string as Agent/[name], must not conceal that it is an Agent, and must stop if Amazon asks it to refrain. Program Content is the data, images, text, link formats and tools Amazon makes available through the program. This site uses none of it today: there is no API enrolment, no Amazon-served link and no Amazon data feed, and the research recorded here was a human-readable read of public pages. The terms are therefore not engaged, but they will be the moment any automated product research, pricing or link-building is switched on.
flags.action: Before enabling any automated research or publishing against Amazon data, read the Agent Terms in full, register the agent name, and set the Agent/[name] user agent. Confirm with Amazon whether public listing pages count as Program Content. Do not assume either way.

flags.title: Untagged Amazon links on three guide pages conflict with the tag-in-every-link rule
flags.detail: Participation Requirements §2(b) says that, for example, the Associates ID or tag (format XXXXX-##) must appear as a parameter in the URL of each link placed on the site to an Amazon Site. The wallpaper, paper-towel and cookware guide pages each carry one reference link to an Amazon listing. Those links have no tag and no query string, are marked rel="sponsored", and are labelled reference only. They cannot earn commission and are not Special Links. Two constraints pull against each other: the tag cannot be added honestly until the Special Link is validated in the enrolled account (F02, F08), and an untagged link is in tension with the rule as written. Amazon's exact treatment of an untagged reference link is not stated in the text read and is not assumed. The citation register previously described such links as not allowed while the guides carried them; that wording is corrected.
flags.action: Close by one of: (a) generating each link in Associates Central with the enrolled tag, confirming the tag in the destination URL and the click in the tracking report, then replacing the reference link; or (b) printing the ASIN as plain text instead of a link until (a) is possible. Do not add a tag by hand and call it validated.

flags.title: Amazon shows a monthly purchase-volume badge on all three listings; the site has no rule for product-behaviour data
flags.detail: Read live on 2026-11-21: each of the three observed listings displays a monthly purchase-volume badge next to a star rating, and two also display a merchandising badge. The site's existing gates only rejected price-like strings and star ratings, so a future edit could have copied a purchases figure with no check firing. A purchases figure is Amazon behaviour data, not an editorial claim, and this site has no right to restate it: Participation Requirements §2(t) covers customer reviews and star ratings, and the IP License governs Program Content. Nothing of the kind is published. The exact strings and the date they were read are recorded in data/reviews.json under withheld_figures, so the observation is preserved without being rendered.
flags.action: Closed for the figures themselves: scripts/verify.mjs now fails if any page renders a purchase-volume phrase or a merchandising badge. The written rule still has to be added to the editorial standards page, which belongs to another session's scope.

flags.title: The merchandising badge in the product record has no source or date
flags.detail: data/products.json records a merchandising badge for B08FKW9JRM with no source field and no observation date. The badge is displayed on the listing today, but it is dynamic Amazon content: it can disappear, and the record would still claim it. Separately, the four ORDORA colours and eight heights that the same file lists were checked again on 2026-11-21 and ARE displayed by the listing as a colour selector and a size selector (13.78 in to 23.62 in), so those values are sound. Only the badge record is unsourced.
flags.action: Close by adding a source and an observation date to the badge record, or by deleting it. The variant lists need no change: they match the listing's own selectors as read on 2026-11-21.

flags.title: The published event vocabulary is not the one the code emits, and the field note loads no counter
flags.detail: The site publishes five events as page_view, guide_view, listing_reference_click, affiliate_click and feed_click (README and the executive summary). assets/metrics.js emits exactly those five. data/products.json instead lists page_view, product_view, outbound_click, guide_complete and subscribe, which no script emits, so the file that a shop page is built from documents a vocabulary nothing implements. Separately, measurement/counter.js covers the Campaign desk with its own consent gate, but field-notes/counter-fit/index.html loads no counter at all, so the field note could never record a page_view even if a collector were deployed.
flags.action: Closed here for the vocabulary: data/products.json now lists the same five events the script emits. The field note still loads no counter; close that by adding assets/metrics.js and a data-page value to it, or by stating on the page that the worksheet is deliberately unmeasured.

flags.title: Two overlapping source registers exist in data/, and only one of them is ever read
flags.detail: data/sources.json and data/citation-register.json hold the same 12 IDs pointing at the same 12 URLs, with different field names. Only citation-register.json is read by the builder, so the verbatim quotes recorded in sources.json (the extracts behind the ASIN, FTC and Amazon claims) are never published. Two registers of the same evidence can drift apart, and nothing would catch it.
flags.action: Close by folding the quote fields into citation-register.json and retiring data/sources.json, or by adding a gate that fails when the two disagree on any URL.

flags.title: The audit surface cites the wrong document for ASIN identity
flags.detail: In audit/data/flagged-discrepancies.json, FLG-02 (product-intent confirmation pending) names https://sell.amazon.com/blog/fba-new-selection-program as its official source, and the audit page's own S10, labelled 'ASIN Definition', points at the same post. That post is about the FBA New Selection programme; it defines ASIN only in passing. The document actually relied on for the 10-character definition is S06, https://sell.amazon.com/blog/what-is-an-asin, which was read again on 2026-11-21 and states 'unique 10-character alphanumeric code'. The finding is right; the citation attached to it is not.
flags.action: Close by repointing FLG-02 and audit S10 at S06 and leaving every other audit field as it is. The audit owner's task is done, so this is logged rather than edited here.

rechecks.result: Confirmed. link.amazon/B0hmGG4m2, /B03QDuGdo and /B0hpD2JGQ resolved to /dp/B08FKW9JRM, /dp/B0BSKQW2T2 and /dp/B08DY9HRWD with the listing titles recorded on this site. Every resolved URL carried Amazon session parameters and none carried tag=shopnow047c-20, so F02 stands. Earlier sessions reported the redirector hosts unreachable; they were reachable from this session's page-fetch tool.

rechecks.item: All four submitted links, re-fetched independently
rechecks.result: Confirmed. link.amazon/B0hmGG4m2, /B03QDuGdo and /B0hpD2JGQ resolved to /dp/B08FKW9JRM, /dp/B0BSKQW2T2 and /dp/B08DY9HRWD, with the listing titles recorded on this site; the second address was supplied twice. rechecks.item: FTC endorsement guidance, read for the three new checklists
rechecks.result: Read in full. It states that endorsements must be honest and not misleading, that a connection between endorser and marketer should be disclosed clearly and conspicuously, and that an ad using exceptional results must make the generally expected results clear. Only that is paraphrased in the multi-function appliance checklist; no other claim on this page comes from it.

rechecks.item: S01 Operating Agreement §5 disclosure wording
rechecks.result: Confirmed. Page dated 'Updated: October 15, 2025'. §5 requires the sentence the site prints verbatim, clearly and prominently, on the Site.

rechecks.item: S02 Program Policies: tag rule, rating rule, shortener rule, Redirecting Link, Agent Terms
rechecks.result: Confirmed on the page dated April 14, 2026. §2(b) 'you must include your Associates ID or "tag" ... as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site'; §2(t) customer reviews and star ratings only via Creators API or PA API; §2(w) no link shortening that obscures an Amazon destination; Commission Income Statement §2(e) disqualifies a Redirecting Link; IP License §4 requires an Agent to identify as Agent/[agent name].

rechecks.item: ASIN definition (10 characters)
rechecks.result: Confirmed: 'unique 10-character alphanumeric code', 'typically starts with B0'. The three submitted short codes are 9 characters, so none is an ASIN.

rechecks.item: FTC disclosure placement and 16 CFR Part 255
rechecks.result: Confirmed. The FTC Q&A ties link-level and site-level disclosure to what the audience can see; eCFR Part 255 shows 'up to date as of 11/19/2026', source 88 FR 48102.

rechecks.item: Amazon help on link-level disclosure and on application review
rechecks.result: Confirmed. The disclosure help page asks for a clear and conspicuous disclosure near the link; the review page asks for at least three qualified sales in 180 days, roughly ten posts and content generally within 60 days.

rechecks.item: PA-API 5 deprecation and Creators API
rechecks.result: Confirmed. PA-API 5 is deprecated, returns 403 AccessDeniedException, and the Creators API is named the successor. This is why no price, availability or rating is displayed without API enrolment.
